title: test-0017-SCI-CHM-SEPARATION
passage: In our science experiments, we often separate mixtures using different physical methods. When we mix sand and salt, we cannot use a sieve to separate them because both particles are small enough to pass through the holes together. Instead, we dissolve the mixture in water and use filtration. Filtration separates insoluble solids like sand from the liquid, but it cannot catch dissolved substances like salt, which pass through the filter paper along with the water. Once we have the salt solution, we can recover the salt through evaporation. During this process, the water turns into steam and disappears, but the salt remains behind as a solid residue. It is important to remember that there is a limit to how much salt can dissolve in a fixed amount of water at a specific temperature. Once this limit is reached, we call it a saturated solution. If we want to dissolve more salt, we must increase the temperature of the water, which allows a larger amount of the substance to dissolve. Stirring only helps the salt dissolve faster, but it does not change the total amount that can be dissolved. Finally, when we see water droplets on the outside of a cold glass, it is not leaking through the metal; it is water vapor from the air turning into liquid droplets upon touching the cold surface.
summary: Remember that there is a limit to how much salt can dissolve in a fixed amount of water at a specific temperature. If we want to dissolve more salt, we need to heat up the water, so that more of the substance can dissolve.
